context_summary: PostHog's leverage this window sat in the correctness of its data-ingestion paths more than in new feature surface. Product: Warehouse sources holds 15.2% of major episodes (`area[Product: Warehouse sources].major_share`), but its 18.7% PR share is inflated by ~864 templated add-source/table PRs, and its two leading authors (C14, 87.7% of his work there; C01, 93.8%) carry 130 and 32 major episodes, so the area reads as two people's output rather than a company-wide theme; changelog counts mislead in the same way, because one '44 new MCP tools' entry is counted in many areas. The densest important work is where the changelog barely looks: Django platform has 10.9% of major episodes on 4.4% of PRs (`area[Django platform (API/models/auth)]`), and the three ingestion areas (nodejs CDP 8.4%, rust 2.9%, personhog 1.9%) hold 13.2% of major work with zero changelog entries, which is where C09, C20, C16 and C05 fixed silent data loss. The second priority was securing the identity and credential surface as AI agents connect to PostHog: C04 (13 security majors), C18 (37 major episodes), C19, C09, C11 and C01 all closed auth, OAuth/MCP or credential-leak holes, and C14's credentials service moved integration secrets for 21 products (#124844, #125029). Structurally, community 1 (purity 0.176) holds seven candidates, the devex, security and frontend-platform core, and four of the top bridges (C04 0.0792, C22 0.0776, C11 0.0556, C12 0.0418); no area has a single point of approval, but the largest stream has one at person level: C15 reviewed 778 and C01 205 of C14's PRs, and 46 of C01's 76 majors had only bot approval. Because 40% of human-authored PRs were approved only by an AI bot (audit note 6), I weighted post-merge behaviour (reverts, follow-up fixes, self-repair chains) and the criticality of specific PRs above first-pass rates and approval centrality.

His record is among the cleanest at high volume (0.983, 0 reverts) and his 24 change requests on others' PRs were 95% adopted, the strongest corrective review signal in the pool.

He also fixed a production OAuth incident (#83929), integration-token loss (#108163, P=16.0) and six access-control leaks (#102477). His quality is below median (0.952, 13 follow-ups), but none touched a major PR and his latest repo-wide ORM change (#126463) is too new to judge, which is why he sits below C07.

In three days he removed compromised eMudhra roots from every runtime PostHog ships (#121580, #121626, #122294), and he moved the app to an enforced CSP on signed-in, shared and embedded pages (#106238, #116719). His 37 major episodes are 2nd of 22, although his review weight is low and the CSP rollout needed ~24 repair PRs.
